.DISCUSSION...
As of 220 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A warming trend is expected through Thursday 
with mostly dry conditions.

Latest surface analysis shows 1026 mb high pressure offshore of
the lower Mid-Atlantic coast, ridging southwest across the Deep
South. Aloft, a broad upper-level ridge remains anchored across
the southern third of the CONUS. To the north, low pressure 
continues to track across northern Ontario toward Quebec, 
pushing an attendant surface cold front south-southwest across 
the Upper Great Lakes and upper Midwest into the mid- Missouri 
Valley.

Mainly sunny early this afternoon with only scattered fair-
weather cumulus. 18Z temperatures are largely in the low to mid 
80s across the region, w/ breezy south-southwest winds gusting
to 15-20 kt. As the surface high drifts farther offshore 
tonight, light but steady return flow will keep temperatures 
slightly milder but still comfortable. Look for overnight lows 
dropping into the mid to upper 60s inland, low 70s along the 
coast, under a mainly clear sky.

The northern upper trough and associated surface low will 
slowly shift east-southeast tonight and Thursday, gradually 
suppressing the ridge. The cold front approaches from the 
northwest tomorrow, slowing as the boundary aligns parallel to 
the mid- and upper-level quasi-zonal flow. Compressional heating
ahead of the front will yield the warmest day of the period on 
Thursday, with highs reaching the low-to-mid 90s inland from the
immediate coast. Recent 12Z guidance trends slightly higher for
isolated to widely scattered convection entering western areas 
late Thursday afternoon, spreading across the Virginia Northern 
Neck and Maryland Lower Eastern Shore Thursday night into early 
Friday.

KEY MESSAGE 2: An unsettled pattern develops late Thursday into
the weekend, with daily chances for showers or thunderstorms.

The dampening mid to upper trough will push the slow-moving 
front across the region late tomorrow night into early Friday 
morning. The boundary likely becomes stalled near or just south
of the Albemarle Sound by midday Friday. A few showers or 
storms remain possible along the boundary over southern 
locations Friday into Friday evening.

Better areawide storm chances arrive Saturday as the stalled 
front lifts back north and a few weak perturbations push across
the region. Considerable cloud cover and scattered to numerous
showers and storms, including the potential for some locally 
heavy downpours, will cap Saturday's highs in the low to mid 80s
for most, with upper 80s limited to the southern third of the 
CWA. There remains an area wide ERO that could suggest some
potential hydro issues in the typical spots for Saturday, given
the moist, modestly unstable airmass and relatively slow steering
flow.

The front washes out late weekend into early next week. Some
additional showers and storms remain possible Sunday, though 
coverage will be noticeably lighter than Saturday. Looking 
ahead, PoPs return back closer to climo normal Sun-Mon, trending
drier through the middle of next week. Meanwhile, the rebuilding
SE ridge/rising heights look to portend a period of near to 
above normal temperatures for the first half of next week.

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
As of 725 PM EDT Wednesday...

VFR conditions across area terminals will persist through the
00z/09 TAF period. High pressure is located off the mid-
Atlantic coast leading to a mainly clear sky and SSW winds ~8-10
knots. Mainly clear skies/VFR conditions will continue through
tonight and much of Thursday.

Outlook: The next chc for showers/tstms arrives later 
Thursday evening into Thursday night as a cold front approaches
from the north. This will also bring the potential for some 
short- lived MVFR CIGs across mainly northern terminals Thu 
night into Friday morning. The boundary slowly drops south 
through Friday morning, but lingers near the VA/NC border Friday
afternoon through early Sunday, with daily chances of 
showers/storms (highest chances southeastern terminals and 
greatest on Saturday). MVFR (LCL IFR) CIGs will also be possible
from PHF- ORF-ECG Friday night into Saturday morning, with 
additional opportunities of sub-VFR CIGs/VSBY in scattered to 
numerous convective showers and embedded t-storms Saturday 
afternoon and evening.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 243 PM EDT Wednesday...

Key Messages:


- S to SW winds increase this afternoon into Thursday. Small  Craft 
Advisories are in effect for the Chesapeake Bay, tidal rivers, and 
northern coastal waters.

- A period of generally benign marine conditions is favored from 
Friday  into early next week.

Afternoon weather analysis shows high pressure sitting off the VA NC 
coast and a cold front portions of the Mid-west. The pressure 
gradient between these two systems has tightened slightly allowing 
for the SSW to increase across the northern bay and coastal waters. 
Winds across those two areas are roughly 15 kt with some gusts 
slowly approaching 20kt. While across the southern bay and coastal 
waters winds are remaining steady around 5-10kt with gusts around 
15kt. Seas are low at this time with 1-2ft waves across the bay and 
2-3 ft across the waters. Through this afternoon and into tomorrow 
morning the pressure gradient is expected to increase as the cold 
front approached from the west. In addition a decently strong LLJ is 
likely to move over the waters. This will help for winds to increase 
over the waters. Winds are expected to increase to around 20 kt 
sustained with gusts between 25-30kt out of the SW. The greatest 
confidence for the 25-30kt gusts are across the far northern bay and 
the coastal waters Cape Charles and north. Elsewhere winds will 
expected to be around 15kt with gusts around 20kt. Small Craft 
Advisories remain in effect for the bay and northern coastal waters 
and have been expanded to the tidal rivers and Cape Charles north. 
During this time expect seas to increase to 3-4ft seas across the 
bay and 3-4ft across the coastal waters with possible 5ft seas 
across the northern coastal waters. With the winds remaining SW 
through the evening elevated seas are likely in he 20-60NM across 
the north with seas likely building to 5-7ft. 

By the late morning tomorrow, the pressure gradient will weaken 
slightly allowing for winds to decrease below SCA criteria. 
Southwest winds will likely drop off to 10-15 kt with gusts nearing 
20 kt nearshore and 25kt offshore. These conditions are likely to 
continue throughout Thursday and into Thursday evening. Seas will 
are likely to remain sub-sca with 1-2ft across the bay and 3-4ft 
across the coastal waters. The cold front is expected to push 
through late Thursday. This could potentially bring a round of 
marginal SCA conditions across the southern coastal waters and 
sound. However, confidence is low at this time. Winds gradually 
become NE 5- 10 kt Fri afternoon as high pressure builds in north of 
the local waters. The flow becomes onshore Fri night into Sat with 
10-15 kt winds possible Sat. Otherwise, a period of generally benign 
marine conditions is favored from Fri into early next week.

Low rip currents are forecasted through the next couple of days. 
However, the surf maybe choppy due to the increase in winds.
